retro_application: This card restates the rule that governed batches 1 and 2, so that it has one implemented home instead of a copy in each decision file and a third in search_replay.py. It changes no verdict: every role below is the role that batch's registration already carried. Any change to a value or a role is a rule change -- register it before the labels it will be read against are collected, and it governs only measurements taken after that date. The two decision files stay the record of what was registered when and of the reasoning; this card is the single implemented source and they cite it.

version_history.change: comparison_universe.denominator becomes confirmable; minimum_sample becomes 100 confirmable (was 300 judged); the primary gate moves from +0.05 absolute to +0.30 SD of the paired differences, with the absolute bar kept as a reported line; query_construction.min_confirmable_queries is set to 100.
version_history.verdict_impact: none on batches 1 and 2: they were read under the 1.0/1.1 values and are not re-read. The new values govern only queries whose labels do not exist yet. Registered in benchmarks/search_eval_decisions_round3.md before that batch's labels are collected, which is the order this card requires.

version_history.change: query_construction.min_confirmable_queries is now read (inert while null, fails closed when the count cannot be verified), every run records labels_sha256, --compare marks the reported counts with the labels revision it could verify, and unknown card fields are refused.
version_history.verdict_impact: none: no gate value or role changed. Both batches were read under 1.0's values, which 1.1 restates unchanged.

version_history.change: first card: restated the rule that governed batches 1 and 2 as a single implemented source.

history.note: Batch 1 registered the rule; its 2026-09-21 section added the minimum effect. Batch 2 registered the sample size, demoted the sign test and fixed two drifts between the registration and this module. Neither file restates the whole rule, so a third batch had to stack two deltas by hand to learn what it was being read against.

definition.judged: every query that has a label row and a result in both runs. A query whose relevant set is empty still counts, as a zero -- it is a measurement of the retriever, not an absence of one.
definition.confirmable: the subset of judged queries whose relevant set is non-empty: the queries where the two arms can differ at all.
definition.discordant: the subset of judged queries where the two arms actually differ (wins + losses).

does_not_apply_to: per-query level metrics: nDCG@5 and the secondary means are reported over every judged query, because a query with nothing to find still measures the retriever
comparison_universe.note: Batches 1 and 2 were both read under `judged`, and batch 2 is why the change is registered rather than assumed: on `judged` its primary mean difference was diluted by 268 of 333 queries that had nothing to find, so the +0.05 absolute bar landed at 0.41 SD there against 0.18 SD on batch 1 -- one rule, two different demands. `confirmable` is fixed by the union of the two arms' pools, so it does not depend on which arm is being looked at. The judged-level mean is still reported beside it, because the gap between the two IS the share of unsatisfiable queries. Governing registration: benchmarks/search_eval_decisions_round3.md.

primary_mean_difference.unit: absolute nDCG@5, mean of paired differences
primary_mean_difference.source: search_eval_decisions.md 规则修正 (2026-09-21), restated in search_eval_decisions_round2.md 3
primary_mean_difference.note: Reported, not gated, from 1.2: it is kept because batches 1 and 2 were read against it. It is not comparable across query compositions (0.18 SD on batch 1, 0.41 SD on batch 2).

primary_mean_difference_sd.note: The gate from 1.2, in SD units so the bar does not move with the query composition. 0.30 SD with 100 confirmable queries gives about 85% power at two-sided alpha=0.05 (about 65% at batch 2's 65 confirmable). The SD is of the paired differences over the same universe.

bootstrap_ci.source: batch 1, kept by batch 2 as the only significance gate

sign_test.note: It reads only signs and needs ~780 discordant pairs at the observed win rate, so requiring it would fail a run on a condition the registration had already dropped.

minimum_sample.note: Was 300 with denominator `judged`, which any label set of 300 queries passed even when none of them had a page to find (batch 2: 65 confirmable). 100 confirmable is the smaller, honest floor for that composition.

effect_calibration.note: Recorded so a third batch re-derives the bar and the sample against its own composition instead of inheriting numbers that were computed for another one. `empty_relevant` is the share of judged queries that cannot show a difference at all.

query_construction.note: min_confirmable_queries is 100 from 1.2. It is enforced twice on purpose: once as the sample gate's value over a confirmable universe, and once here, which survives a future batch that moves the denominator back to `judged`. min_new_queries stays a construction rule for the person building the query set, not a gate -- the harness cannot refuse queries it was never given, so the known-key guard is what keeps that visible.
